newsitem.title: GERMANY: Mannesmann cuts D2 mobile phone rates.
newsitem.headline: Mannesmann cuts D2 mobile phone rates.

text.p: Mannesmann AG, joining a price war among German mobile phone operators, said on Wednesday it would cut rental rates and call charges for users of its Mannesmann Mobilfunk GmbH unit's D2 network.

Following up on rate cuts announced last week by Deutsche Telekom AG, operator of the competing D1 network, Mannesmann said the reductions were part of its strategy to boost its business among private customers.

Mannesmann said it was cutting charges on a peak call on its D2-Classic package by 30 pfennigs to 99 pfennigs a minute, while leaving activation charges and monthly fees unchanged at 99 marks and 69.95 marks respectively.

It also said it was halving the monthly rental on its D2-Fun deal to 24.95 marks, leaving call charges unchanged at 1.89 marks peak rate and 39 pfennigs off-peak. The activation fee remains unchanged at 99 marks.

Mannesmann Mobilfunk chief executive Juergen von Kuczkowski said the cuts were aimed at growth: "We are further pursuing the course we took last year with the launch of the D2-Fun tariff, moving towards bulk business," he told reporters.

The new rates take effect from October 30 and the minimum contract period will be two years. Customers wanting to switch packages will have to pay a fee, unless they have had a D2 phone for over two years.

Mannesmann's strategy of tailoring its mobile phone deals differently to high-volume users and those in Germany who regard their "handy" as a glamorous accessory has succeeded in winning around 80,000 new customers a month.
That has cut into the market share of the D1 network, and Telekom's decision to cut rental fees to 29 marks a month from 49 marks last week was seen by analysts as a defensive move.

Mannesmann Mobilfunk, owned by Mannesmann and AirTouch Communications of the United States, will still enjoy a noticeable increase in turnover this year despite the price cuts, Kuczkowski told reporters.
Cuts in the D2-Fun renetal will result in a fall of around 20 percent in turnover per customer -- but that would be offset by increases in customers. D2 now has 2.2 million subscribers.
Kuczkowski said investment would total 800 million marks this year and a similar amount next year.
Total investment to the end of 1995 was 2.5 billion marks, going towards expanding the network to cope with increasing subscriber numbers.
